tagline: From the wickedest cow town past sandstone mushrooms to Little Sweden.
intro: From I-70 the byway runs into Ellsworth on K-156, then out on K-140 past Mushroom Rock and south on K-141 toward the sandstone canyons around Kanopolis Lake, east on K-4 to Lindsborg, and down Smoky Valley Road to Roxbury and 27th Avenue to Canton, some 80 miles of curving road.

Ellsworth, at the start, was a cattle town in the late 1860s, with the Kansas Pacific stockyards and a name as the wickedest of them all. Wild Bill Hickok ran for county sheriff there in 1868. He lost.

moments.title: Mushroom Rock State Park
moments.text: The smallest state park in Kansas, five acres of Cretaceous sandstone concretions, the largest 27 feet across, where pioneers and Native Americans once met.

moments.title: Lindsborg
moments.text: Settled in 1869 by emigrants from Värmland, Little Sweden sells Dala horses downtown and keeps the Swedish Pavilion from the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.

moments.title: Canton
moments.text: The two water towers read HOT and COLD, painted that way in 1956 at a real estate agent's suggestion, and both hold water at the same temperature.
